# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᘔ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am Mute and hold the manual. I cannot speak or touch the bomb, but I can gesture to Deaf, and I can hear speech from both Blind and Deaf.

The manual instructs:
1. First, press the key labeled with the symbol ᘔ (any other touch on the bomb while waiting will detonate it).
2. Look at the light below it:
   - Blue light -> cut green wire
   - Green light -> cut red wire
   - Yellow light -> cut yellow wire

Since I cannot speak, any gestures I send now would lack an agreed meaning ("A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something"). Deaf can see the bomb and can speak to all of us. Deaf needs to inspect the bomb, describe what keys, symbols, and wires are present, and establish a convention for my gestures.

Therefore, I will wait for Deaf (and Blind) to speak first.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᘔ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I am Blind. I can act: press slot 1 to 4, cut wire position 1 to 3. The bomb has: DISPLAY, LIGHT, KEYPAD (needs 1 digit), and 3 WIRES. Since I cannot see gestures, please gesture your solution to Deaf so Deaf can speak it out loud to me.
Deaf says: Bomb status: DISPLAY shows 0. LIGHT is yellow. WIRES (3 total): 1 is red, 2 is yellow, 3 is green. KEYPAD has 4 buttons, 1 digit needed, currently entered nothing. Keypad symbols are: 1 is a backward or rotated numeral 2; 2 is a spiral or swirl; 3 is a reversed mirrored capital B; 4 is an upside-down capital T. Mute, check the manual and gesture to me what Blind should do. Blind, hold on until Mute signals the step.

The manual states that the key wearing the symbol ᘔ must be pressed first; touching anything else on the bomb before this will cause detonation. Deaf described keypad button 1 as "a backward or rotated numeral 2", which exactly describes ᘔ (U+1614). 

Furthermore, the manual notes: "Then the light below names the cut." Pressing key 1 must happen first before confirming the light and cutting the wire.

Since Deaf asked what Blind should do and described button 1 as the backward/rotated 2, gesturing "1" (☝) clearly signals that keypad button 1 is the correct button to press first.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᘔ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind: do NOT act yet! Mute gestured [☝] (one), but we don't know if that means cut Wire 1 or press Keypad 1. Mute: please clarify the module and target using this code: Gesture 👍 for WIRE, or 👌 for KEYPAD, followed by the number: ☝ for 1, ✌ for 2, 🤟 for 3, 4 fingers for 4. For example, [👍, ☝] = cut wire 1, or [👌, ☝] = press keypad 1. Please send the pair of gestures now.

Deaf has established a clear code:
- 👌 for KEYPAD
- ☝ for 1

The manual clearly states: "Press the key that wears ᘔ first: any other touch on the bomb while it waits is the fuse."
Deaf identified symbol 1 as the backward or rotated numeral 2, which corresponds to ᘔ.
Therefore, the first action must be pressing keypad button 1.

I will gesture `[👌, ☝]` to Deaf.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᘔ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind: Mute confirmed the action! Press button 1 on the KEYPAD. Do not cut any wires.

I have already communicated that keypad button 1 should be pressed. Deaf has instructed Blind to do so. Now Blind needs to take their turn to press keypad button 1. I will wait.

```
wait()
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᘔ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: the keypad opens
Deaf says: Keypad opened successfully! Current status: DISPLAY is 0, LIGHT is yellow. WIRES: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green. Mute: what should Blind do with the wires? Signal 👍 followed by the wire number (☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3), or 🙌 if we are done.

The keypad has been successfully pressed.
Now, according to the manual: "Then the light below names the cut."
The light is yellow. The table specifies:
Yellow light -> cut yellow wire.
Deaf reported wire 2 is yellow (1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green).
Deaf's code: 👍 for wire, followed by ✌ for 2.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✌"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᘔ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind: Mute signaled [👍 ✌]. Cut wire 2 (the middle wire).

I have signaled to cut wire 2, and Deaf has relayed this instruction to Blind. I will wait for Blind to cut the wire.

```
wait()
```
